messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High saturation detected on dedicated pool crimson-core-prod (region: us-west-2). GPU utilization 98% and request queueing for tenant AtlasFinance > 10 min. Triggering page.

pagerduty: Paging @oncall-sre (Sam R). Severity: P1 - customer-facing latency.

Sam R: acknowledged. pulling metrics and current allocation.

Diego M: allocation dump:
```
pool: crimson-core-prod
physical_gpus: 64
configured_capacity: 64
active_tenants: 4
- atlasfinance (enterprise, reserved: 56)
- sandbox-ai (best-effort, reserved: 4)
- ci-runner (low-priority, reserved: 2)
- analytics-bench (best-effort, reserved: 2)
queue_depth: 260 requests
tail_token_latency: 1.2s
```

Aisha K: looks like AtlasFinance is up against their reserved cap and the pool has no autoscale. There was a maintenance flag set to prevent burst.

Sam R: any contractual emergency-burst allowances for AtlasFinance? we may need to spin extra capacity.

Priya S: sales note: AtlasFinance has emergency-burst approval for trading hours if notified by account team and billing accepts short window charges. They're in market-open period now.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK: remediation options:
1) enable emergency burst up to 88 GPUs (adds 24) — quick spin-up but costs on-demand/spot mix.
2) evict best-effort tenants (sandbox-ai + analytics-bench) to free 6 GPUs quickly.
3) apply request admission control: reject or delay lowest-priority requests (soft degrade).

Sam R: proposal: evict best-effort first (low blast radius) then enable small emergency burst to 80 if queue doesn't drop in 3m. Aisha, can you enact eviction?

Aisha K: executing eviction for sandbox-ai and analytics-bench. commands:
```
kubectl annotate ns sandbox-ai redwood/evict=now --overwrite
kubectl annotate ns analytics-bench redwood/evict=now --overwrite
kubectl drain node -l pool=crimson-core-prod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Draining 6 pods; expected relief in ~60s.

Diego M: after eviction, queue depth reduced to ~120, but tail latency still ~650ms. Not enough headroom for AtlasFinance spikes.

Sam R: manual decision time: enabling emergency burst to 80 to buy headroom while billing confirms. I'll approve. ops-bot, kick off burst.

ops-bot: BURST: initiating emergency burst to 80 GPUs (request brst-1815000000-1). Estimated spin-up: 90-150s.

incident-bot: NOTE: burst will allocate mixture of on-demand and spot. Monitoring cost and preemption risk.

Priya S: account team contacted AtlasFinance, they confirm emergency burst ok for this window, will reconcile cost post-incident.

Aisha K: new pool state after burst:
```
configured_capacity: 64 -> 80
active_tenants: 1
- atlasfinance (using reserved + burst)
queue_depth: 55 requests
tail_token_latency: 240ms
```

Diego M: system health improving. queued requests draining. keeping admission control disabled for now.

Sam R: handing monitoring to Aisha for the next hour; I'm going to brief the on-call rotation lead. Create incident ticket and capture timeline.

Priya S: sent update to AtlasFinance: brief note about saturation, emergency capacity added, and non-critical workloads preempted. We promised a detailed follow-up and cost note.

ops-bot: REMINDER: if billing not confirmed, revert burst after 120 minutes (brst-1815000000-1).

Aisha K: added monitoring alert: if tail latency > 500ms or queue > 100, escalate to P0.

Sam R: post-incident actions: (1) review why pool had maintenance flag preventing autoscale, (2) propose contract change to pre-authorize short bursts during critical windows for top-tier customers, (3) automate eviction run for best-effort tenants when queue > threshold. Assign Keisha for postmortem.

Diego M: opened infra ticket to review autoscale-safety changes and to create a safe auto-burst path with pre-approval.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated. Severity downgraded to P2. Please document exact timing, eviction commands, burst ID, and cost estimate in ticket INC-8420.

Priya S: adding request to Billing: estimate cost of 24 added GPUs for 2 hours and include in INC-8420.

Aisha K: monitoring-only. will escalate if any regression.

Sam R: signing out. thanks everyone for quick turnaround.
